use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: To originate and report real-time air and surface (maritime) tracks using the J3.2 and J3.3 surveillance messages.

goal.raw_text: To originate and report real-time air and surface (maritime) tracks using the J3.2 and J3.3 surveillance messages.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has an automatic correlation capability for air and surface tracks.
The C2 JU has an automatic decorrelation capability for real-time air or surface tracks it initiates.
The C2 JU has the capability to perform common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria.
Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration have been performed.
After initially achieving Active status or returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, the minimum wait of 12 seconds before reporting air and surface tracks has elapsed.
A C2 JU initiates a real-time air or surface track.

trigger.raw_text: A C2 JU initiates a real-time air or surface track.

claims.content: The C2 JU, having the capability to originate and report real-time air or surface tracks, performs common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria.

In common tracking, the C2 JU shares a common track number and shifting R^2 between C2 JUs; each air, surface (maritime), land (ground), and space tracked object is normally reported by one C2 JU while other C2 JUs withhold their reports to prevent cluttering the tactical plot.
The C2 JU commences the correlation process by comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with data received on the interface to prevent or eliminate dual designations.
The C2 JU periodically compares remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
When the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually.
The C2 JU reports Air surveillance data using the J3.2 (PTI = 1) message and Surface (Maritime) surveillance data using the J3.3 (PTI = 1) message.
For Air surveillance reporting, the C2 JU includes Altitude and Altitude Source when available.

The C2 JU reports the velocity of Air and Surface (Maritime) tracks as course and speed, with speed reported in data miles per hour of ground speed and course reported in degrees with respect to true north.
The C2 JU exchanges track identity as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1.
At main flow step 0, the C2 JU may also perform manual decorrelation, and may have a capability to require manual confirmation of automatic decorrelations.

At main flow step 4, if a correlation request is rejected, the C2 JU transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

At main flow step 5, if the C2 JU does not have R^2, it is responsible for monitoring IFF/SIF surveillance data and only reporting if it holds different data with the J7.5 message; the JU with R^2 reports all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for that track in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages.

At main flow step 5, if the C2 JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has R^2, it transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, except when it ceases reporting because it has relinquished R^2 to another JU or when that track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.
If a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection. Exit: the rejection is reported via J7.2.

After initially achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, C2 JUs capable of assuming R^2 for air, surface, or land tracks shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed; the minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds. Exit: transmission is withheld until those checks and the minimum wait are complete.

For IFF/SIF surveillance data reporting, all JUs without R^2 are responsible for monitoring such data and only reporting if they hold different data with the J7.5 message. Exit: if different data are held, report them with J7.5; otherwise continue monitoring and do not report.
Air surveillance data is reported using the J3.2 (PTI = 1) message.
Surface (Maritime) surveillance data is reported using the J3.3 (PTI = 1) message.
Air surveillance reporting includes Altitude and Altitude Source when available.

The velocity of Air and Surface (Maritime) tracks is reported as course and speed, with speed reported in data miles per hour of ground speed and course reported in degrees with respect to true north.
Track identity is exchanged as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1.
